Syria.summary: Syria's displacement crisis began in 2011 when peaceful protests against President Bashar al-Assad's government were met with violent crackdowns, igniting a civil war that would become one of the most devastating of the 21st century. More than 13 years later, it remains the world's largest protracted displacement situation.
causes: Armed conflict and civil war
Government crackdowns and airstrikes
Rise of ISIS and extremist groups
Economic collapse and hyperinflation
Destruction of civilian infrastructure

timeline.event: Arab Spring protests erupt; government responds with force, sparking civil war
Displacement crosses 2 million as fighting intensifies across major cities
Mass Mediterranean crossings; European refugee crisis peaks
Idlib offensive displaces 900,000 in three months — fastest displacement since WWII
February earthquake kills 50,000+ and displaces hundreds of thousands more

Ukraine.summary: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022 triggered the fastest displacement crisis in Europe since World War II. Within weeks, millions had fled westward. Though some have returned, millions remain displaced inside Ukraine or abroad — many uncertain if they can ever go home.
causes: Russian full-scale military invasion
Aerial bombardment of cities and infrastructure
Occupation of eastern and southern territories
Destruction of civilian homes and energy systems
Ongoing frontline conflict with no ceasefire

timeline.event: Russia annexes Crimea; conflict begins in Donbas — early displacement begins
Full-scale invasion launches; 10 million displaced within first month
4 million cross into Europe — fastest refugee exodus since WWII
Frontlines stabilise; some returns begin but millions remain displaced
Continued attacks on energy infrastructure drive further internal displacement

Afghanistan.summary: Afghanistan has been in near-continuous conflict for over four decades — from Soviet invasion to civil war, US-led occupation, and Taliban rule. The 2021 Taliban takeover triggered a new wave of displacement, particularly affecting women, journalists, and those who worked with foreign forces or governments.
causes: Taliban takeover and persecution of minorities
Four decades of continuous armed conflict
Severe drought and climate-driven food insecurity
Economic collapse following international sanctions
Suppression of women's rights and civil society

timeline.event: Soviet invasion begins decades of displacement that never fully ended
US-led invasion displaces millions; refugee crisis intensifies
Taliban resurgence drives new displacement waves across the country
Taliban seize Kabul; chaotic evacuation and mass displacement begins
Humanitarian crisis deepens — 20 million face acute food insecurity

South Sudan.summary: South Sudan became the world's newest country in 2011, but independence quickly gave way to ethnic conflict and civil war. Despite a fragile peace agreement signed in 2018, localised violence continues. South Sudan simultaneously hosts refugees from neighbouring countries while producing millions of its own.
causes: Civil war between government and opposition forces
Ethnic and political violence between communities
Collapse of basic services and infrastructure
Climate shocks — floods and drought
Chronic underfunding of humanitarian response

timeline.event: South Sudan declares independence from Sudan
Civil war erupts between President Kiir and former VP Machar
Peace deal collapses; fighting resumes — 4 million displaced
Revitalised peace agreement signed; fighting reduces but continues
Renewed conflict in some states; displacement remains at crisis levels

Myanmar.summary: Myanmar's displacement crisis has two overlapping dimensions: the long-running persecution of the Rohingya Muslim minority — described by the UN as a genocide — and the mass displacement triggered by the 2021 military coup, which plunged the country into civil war.
causes: 2021 military coup and ongoing civil conflict
Decades of Rohingya persecution and statelessness
Military airstrikes on civilian populations
Ethnic armed group conflicts across border regions
Economic collapse following coup

timeline.event: Military 'clearance operations' force 750,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh in weeks
Military coup deposes elected government; protests met with lethal force
Civil war spreads across multiple regions; 600,000 newly displaced
Opposition forces gain ground; fighting intensifies in Shan and Chin states
Over 2 million internally displaced — worst figures since 2021 coup

Sudan.summary: Sudan's crisis exploded in April 2023 when war broke out between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group. What began as a power struggle became one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters — with mass atrocities, famine, and a displacement surge that overtook Syria as the world's largest active crisis.
causes: War between SAF and RSF paramilitary forces
Systematic targeting of civilians and aid workers
Collapse of healthcare and food systems
Historical ethnic tensions in Darfur region
Regional spillover affecting Chad, Egypt and South Sudan

timeline.event: Darfur conflict begins — hundreds of thousands killed, millions displaced
President Omar al-Bashir ousted after 30 years; transition government formed
War erupts between SAF and RSF; Khartoum reduced to battleground
7 million displaced in six months — fastest displacement surge ever recorded
Famine declared in parts of Sudan; aid access severely restricted

DR Congo.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has the largest internally displaced population in Africa and one of the world's most chronic and underreported crises. Decades of militia violence, competition for mineral resources, and state fragility have kept millions perpetually displaced across a country the size of Western Europe.
causes: Dozens of armed militia groups operating across eastern DRC
Competition for valuable mineral resources
Weak state institutions and security forces
Regional interference from neighbouring countries
Chronic underfunding — one of the least-reported crises globally

timeline.event: Rwandan genocide spills across border; decades of instability follow
Second Congo War — deadliest conflict since WWII — displaces millions
M23 rebel group seizes Goma; mass displacement in North Kivu
M23 resurgence backed by Rwanda; 800,000 displaced in months
6.9 million IDPs — Africa's largest internal displacement crisis

Somalia.summary: Somalia has endured over three decades of state collapse, clan conflict, and Al-Shabaab insurgency. Climate shocks — increasingly severe droughts and floods — compound the crisis, making Somalia one of the clearest examples of how conflict and climate change interact to drive displacement.
causes: Al-Shabaab militant insurgency
Clan-based armed conflict
Severe drought and climate-driven famine
State fragility and governance collapse
Cyclical flooding displacing coastal communities

timeline.event: Government collapses; clan warfare erupts — state has not fully recovered since
Famine kills 260,000; mass displacement to Kenya and Ethiopia
Drought and famine conditions return; 6 million face starvation
Fifth consecutive failed rainy season — worst drought in 40 years
3.8 million IDPs; Al-Shabaab controls significant rural territory

Yemen.summary: Yemen's civil war began in 2015 when a Saudi-led coalition intervened against Houthi forces who had seized the capital. Nearly a decade later, the war has created what the UN calls the world's worst humanitarian crisis — with millions facing famine, disease outbreaks, and a health system in total collapse.
causes: Civil war between government forces and Houthi movement
Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on civilian infrastructure
Blockade of Hodeidah port restricting food imports
Total collapse of public sector and health services
Pre-existing poverty and food insecurity

timeline.event: Houthi forces seize Sanaa; president flees to Saudi Arabia
Saudi-led coalition begins airstrikes; war officially begins
Hodeidah offensive threatens 70% of Yemen's food imports
Truce holds for months — longest pause in fighting since 2015
4.5 million IDPs; 17 million facing acute food insecurity

Ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia's displacement crisis stems from multiple overlapping emergencies — the Tigray War (2020–2022), one of Africa's deadliest recent conflicts, alongside ongoing intercommunal violence in Oromia and Amhara regions, and recurring climate shocks. Peace was signed in 2022 but violence and displacement continue.
causes: Tigray War between federal government and TPLF (2020–2022)
Intercommunal violence in Oromia and Amhara
Severe drought across the Horn of Africa
Political and ethnic tensions across regions
Slow delivery of post-conflict reconstruction

timeline.event: Federal government launches military offensive in Tigray region
Tigray conflict expands into Afar and Amhara; 2 million displaced
Cessation of hostilities agreement signed in Pretoria
Peace process advances but Amhara conflict intensifies
3.5 million IDPs across multiple active conflict zones

Venezuela.summary: Venezuela's crisis is the largest displacement situation in Latin American history and one of the largest globally — driven not by war but by economic collapse, political repression, and the systematic dismantling of public institutions under successive governments. Over 7.7 million have left, mostly on foot.
causes: Economic collapse and hyperinflation destroying livelihoods
Political repression under Maduro government
Collapse of healthcare, education and basic services
Food and medicine shortages
Violence from armed criminal groups (colectivos)

timeline.event: Oil price crash triggers economic collapse; emigration begins accelerating
Hyperinflation exceeds 1,000,000%; mass exodus begins in earnest
Disputed election; US and EU sanctions intensify economic pressure
Venezuela surpasses Syria as largest displacement in the Americas
7.7 million displaced — mostly in Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Chile, Brazil

Palestine.summary: Palestinians represent one of the world's oldest and largest protracted refugee situations. The 1948 Arab-Israeli War displaced over 700,000 Palestinians — an event Palestinians call the Nakba (catastrophe). Their descendants now number nearly 6 million registered refugees. The 2023 Gaza war triggered the most acute displacement since 1948.
causes: 1948 Nakba and subsequent Arab-Israeli conflicts
Israeli occupation of West Bank and Gaza
2023 Gaza war displacing nearly entire population
Blockade of Gaza restricting movement and aid
Statelessness — no recognised Palestinian state

timeline.event: Nakba — 700,000+ Palestinians displaced during Arab-Israeli War
Six-Day War; Israel occupies West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and Golan Heights
Gaza blockade begins after Hamas takes control of the territory
Hamas attack; Israel launches military campaign — 1.9 million displaced in Gaza
Nearly entire Gaza population displaced; humanitarian access severely restricted

Haiti.summary: Haiti's crisis is a compounding of disasters — political collapse following the 2021 presidential assassination, gang control of large swaths of Port-au-Prince, the 2010 earthquake's unresolved legacy, and chronic poverty. Gang violence now drives more displacement than natural disasters.
causes: Gang violence controlling up to 80% of Port-au-Prince
Assassination of President Moïse in 2021
Collapse of state authority and police capacity
Recurrent natural disasters (earthquakes, hurricanes)
Extreme poverty and lack of economic alternatives

timeline.event: Earthquake kills 200,000+ and displaces 1.5 million; recovery remains incomplete
Hurricane Matthew devastates southern Haiti; 175,000 displaced
President Jovenel Moïse assassinated; political vacuum deepens gang power
Gang coalition seizes major infrastructure; 200,000 flee Port-au-Prince
310,000 IDPs; Kenya-led international security mission begins deployment

Colombia.summary: Colombia hosts one of Latin America's largest internally displaced populations — a legacy of five decades of FARC guerrilla conflict, paramilitary violence, and now the continued activity of dissident groups and drug cartels. Colombia also hosts the most Venezuelan refugees and migrants of any country.
causes: Decades of FARC and paramilitary conflict
Dissident FARC groups rejecting 2016 peace deal
Drug cartel territorial violence in rural areas
Hosting 2.9 million Venezuelan refugees
Land disputes and forced displacement of Afro-Colombian and indigenous communities

timeline.event: FARC guerrilla movement founded; begins rural conflict
Peak of conflict — millions displaced by FARC and paramilitary violence
Historic FARC peace deal signed; displacement begins to fall
Venezuelan crisis accelerates; Colombia becomes largest host country
4.9 million IDPs; dissident groups filling FARC's former territories
